queue.li_title: DSCR Cash-Out Refinance Seasoning: 3, 6, and 12 Months
queue.li_desc: Why seasoning windows exist, what they cost investors, and how the 3-month rule changes BRRRR math.
queue.li:
The number that decides how fast a BRRRR investor scales isn't the rehab budget or the ARV. It's the seasoning window.

Most DSCR lenders require 6-12 months of ownership before a cash-out refinance can use the new appraised value. That's 6-12 months of your capital parked in a finished, rented property doing nothing.

Our window is 3 months. No lease required at closing — the market-rent appraisal qualifies.

On a $110K cash-in deal, getting your capital back at month 3 instead of month 6 is the difference between four cycles a year and two. At portfolio scale, that compounds into an entirely different growth curve.

The full math, including the delayed-financing exception: https://slacapital.ai/blog/dscr-cash-out-seasoning/

queue.li_title: Hard Money vs. DSCR Loans: Which One Fits Your Deal?
queue.li_desc: Two tools, two jobs — and the bridge-to-DSCR play that combines them.
queue.li:
Investors ask us which is better — hard money or DSCR. Wrong question. They're different tools for different jobs, and the best operators use both on the same property.

Hard money buys the project: 6-24 months, interest-only, sized off after-repair value, funds the rehab, closes in as little as 72 hours.

DSCR holds the property: 30-year term from 5.75%, qualified on the rent it produces — no tax returns, no DTI.

The combined play is the standard BRRRR sequence: acquire and renovate on bridge, stabilize, refinance into DSCR at month 3, recycle the capital. One lender across both loans means the second underwrite starts warm instead of from scratch.

Full comparison: https://slacapital.ai/blog/hard-money-vs-dscr-loans/
queue.fb:
